adjudications.adopted_text: Every gate condition carries the words 'Deciding run:' or 'Deciding runs:' with the command, the tool and the file it runs on, or 'Deciding record:' with a record and a place in it. A record not yet written when the gate is issued is named by the lane that will write it and the place it will write. A term of art in a condition is defined in the condition or points to the pinned place that defines it. A condition meant to reach below a tool's gate says so in words and names the run that measures there; a condition that names no such run reaches the gate and no further. The brief builder refuses a condition without one of the tokens, and a condition whose named tool or existing file is not among the reviewing lane's pinned inputs; a lane's own script over pinned files is not refused when the condition names it. A refused condition goes back to the ruling that wrote it, not to the reviewer to construe. The check proves that a run is named and pinned; it does not prove that the run answers the condition, which stays the ruling's duty. Measured in 1 Corinthians: one condition with no run of its own drew two required changes and a ruling; four conditions of an earlier ruling stood NOT_TESTABLE at the audit for want of named files with the item above in force, and the records read at the close do not show that item's builder check run; the last ruling wrote a token on all 11 of its conditions, one author's form, and 4 of the 11 name no file. The builder refusal is untried.

adjudications.adopted_text:
**A witness pair: two editions of one language (new, M8, 1 Corinthians).** Where a book has two witnesses of one language, the strategy names one primary and one secondary. Four rules follow, and each that can be checked by its form is installed before the writers run (section 5).

1. Argument runs on the primary. A quotation is sliced from the primary, and the secondary is quoted to disclose and for nothing else. A rival is not rejected on a word the secondary lacks: that rejection is not witness-neutral.
2. A critical sign in the secondary marks a variant site and nothing else. It supports no seam and no confidence. Where no apparatus is staged, the content of the variant is UNAVAILABLE.
3. There are two duties and two checks. (a) Every sign verse inside a row's span is listed in the row as a bare location. (b) A quotation of the primary in a warrant field, at a verse where the pair differ, carries a disclosure of the secondary at that verse when its words fall on or across a sign, or when they are not contiguous in the secondary. A difference verse that no quotation touches owes nothing under (b). A hit under (b) is cleared by hand only where the difference is orthography or the quotation carries no seam or rival argument, with the reason recorded per hit.
4. The strategy names the fields each check reads and says why any field is left out. A quotation standing in a field left out supports no seam and no rejection; one found doing so brings the field back into the check.

Replace the last two sentences of the paragraph above, those beginning 'Daniel tested this' and 'The predicate for a Greek witness', with: 'Daniel tested this with a Hebrew and Aramaic witness and an English one. 1 Corinthians stated a predicate for a Greek witness in its strategy, with its run length and neighbour width ASSUMED, and the records read at its close show no tool for it and no run of it, which does not show that none was run. The next book with a Greek witness installs the predicate as a tool with a must-fail fixture before its writers run.'
adjudications.target_section: §7: new paragraph after the paragraph beginning 'The predicate tells a reader where the tool looks', and that paragraph's last two sentences replaced

adjudications.adopted_text: 5. A round may be applied by a tool with no author when every change in it is a run of prose bytes ordered exactly by a ruling. A row's verse range, a boundary value or a confidence is not changed this way. The ruling role then holds the author's duty under rule 3 for every field it orders, and records it beside the dry run; 1 Corinthians left no such record, so this duty is untried, as rule 3 is. The tool applies each span exactly once and stops on any other count, and the round's record carries the expected digest of the result. The applying tool is pinned to the lane that reviews the round, or that lane rebuilds the result from the ordered spans by its own script and compares bytes. The ruling role wrote those words and ruled on them, so lanes that did not write them read every changed field whole under rule 4 before the close, in the number section 19 requires. This rule does not lower that number and does not settle whether a round of ordered spans may be read by fewer lanes than another round; on the record of its close the last such round in 1 Corinthians was read whole by one audit lane, and that count is not a precedent. Byte equality carries an unchanged row forward and carries nothing else. 1 Corinthians ran two such rounds, 18 spans and 26 spans, with no change outside the spans as its audit reports; the rule rests on those two.

adjudications.adopted_text: **A grammatical label is a claim about a form (new, M8, 1 Corinthians).** A label of mood, case or tense names a form that stands in the words it is put on: a run of witness words given a label holds that form. Where no morphology layer is staged, the label is the writer's reading of the bytes and its tier is INFERRED. A label that carries a seam or the rejection of a rival is replaced by what the form measures (the verse-initial word, a connective-free opening, the person), or it is marked as the writer's reading in the same sentence. A label that carries nothing stays. Where a form is the same in two moods, neither mood is measured, and the seam rests on something else.
